title: Client canary schema validation harness and migration playbook
creator: Hannah Ku
description: Runbook and implementation plan to introduce a client-side canary and server-side validation harness that allow incremental analytics schema changes (SDK, CLI, API) with minimal customer impact. This ticket covers: 1) an opt-in SDK/CLI canary mode that emits both old and new envelopes for sampled traffic, 2) a standalone validation service ("schema-gate") that computes diff statistics and injects reject/accept signals into the routing layer, 3) dashboards and alerts to track mismatch rates and regression signals, and 4) an operator playbook for rollout, rollback, and emergency migrations. The goal is to provide deterministic visibility into forward/backward compatibility issues before enforcing a new schema in the ingestion path.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs and CLI have a flag --telemetry-canary that can be enabled per-token to emit new-schema events in tandem with current-schema events at configurable sample rates
schema-gate service accepts event batches, validates them against both schemas, returns per-batch compatibility metrics, and exposes an API used by the router to apply temporary gating policies
A Grafana dashboard shows schema acceptance rate, field-level drop rates, and clients-by-version heatmap with a 1-minute refresh and a baseline alert if mismatch_rate > 0.5% over 15m
Playbook documented in Confluence with steps for canary enablement, escalation contacts, and rollback commands; tested in staging with a fake-client traffic generator
Automated tests (unit + e2e) that validate SDK flag toggling, CLI dry-run mode, and schema-gate metrics collection are present and green in CI
steps: Design SDK/CLI interface: feature flag name, sampling parameter, telemetry envelope versioning header (X-Telemetry-Schema) - DONE 2025-02-14
Implement SDK shim to duplicate events when canary enabled; ensure KV cache and batching semantics preserved - WIP
Add CLI dry-run mode which prints validation results locally and can emit to a staging schema-gate endpoint
Build schema-gate microservice (Go) with pluggable validators: JSON-Schema + custom rules for required telemetry fields
Integrate schema-gate with router to accept a gating decision API; default is permissive until rollout threshold met
Create Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty runbook for alerting on high mismatch rates
Run staged canary with two internal clients (mobile-app-staging, backend-smoke) at 1% then ramp to 10% over 48h
Capture learnings and update migration playbook; schedule follow-up retro
notes: Trade-offs: duplicating events increases telemetry cost and storage; mitigate by tight sample rates and TTL for canary payloads in S3/GCS
We prefer a soft-fail gating policy by default to avoid customer-facing data loss; enforcement only after 95%+ acceptance across 72h
Validation latency target: schema-gate should process a typical batch < 200ms P95 to avoid routing delays. If exceeded, router falls back to async validation path
Alternative considered: a strict server-side reject policy with client version quarantine. Rejected due to high risk for customers with older SDKs and enterprise deployments
Edge cases: multiplexed batched-envelopes require per-item validation and attribution for accurate per-client stats

risks: Cost: duplicate telemetry increases monthly storage and ingestion costs; finance sign-off required for production ramp
Operational: false positives in validation could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; threshold tuning is critical
Privacy: new schema fields might accidentally surface PII; must run schema-sensitive-field scan before canary enrollment
Compatibility: some legacy CLI users cannot opt-in without a patch; include fallback grace period and server-side compatibility transforms
